Perfect. Here's your checklist in order. The steps follow the regulators' own rules, so you'll need to do them in this sequence to avoid delays.

## Start here

**1. Product composition meets the Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations [1]**
Check that your zobo recipe and ingredients meet NAFDAC's standards for fruit drinks. This is the foundation—NAFDAC won't inspect or register your product if it doesn't meet these rules first.

**2. CAC business registration [2]**
Register your business name with the Corporate Affairs Commission. As a sole proprietor, this is straightforward and usually takes a few days. You'll need this registration before you can apply for most other permits.

**3. Trademark availability search [3]**
Search to make sure your zobo brand name isn't already registered by someone else. This is quick and inexpensive, and you must do it before you file your trademark application.

**4. Food handler medical tests for production staff [1]**
You (and anyone helping you make the drinks) need medical clearance. This is required every year, so you'll need to renew it regularly.

## Once your CAC registration comes through

**5. Production facility meets NAFDAC requirements [1]**
Your kitchen or production space must meet NAFDAC's hygiene and safety standards. Get this sorted before you apply for inspection.

**6. Federal Tax ID [6]**
Register with the Nigeria Revenue Service to get your tax ID number. You'll need this for most other registrations.

**7. Oyo State tax registration [6]**
Register with Oyo State's tax authority as well.

**8. Trademark application (filing) [3]**
File your trademark with the Intellectual Property Office. This protects your brand name.

## Before you open

**9. NAFDAC facility inspection application and inspection [1]**
Apply to NAFDAC to inspect your production facility. They'll check that it meets their hygiene and safety standards. Once they approve, you can move to product testing.

**10. Laboratory analysis of registration samples [1]**
Send samples of your zobo to NAFDAC's lab for testing. They check the composition, safety and shelf life.

**11. NAFDAC product registration [1]**
Once the lab results are good, NAFDAC registers your product. This is your main approval to sell.

**12. Product labelling [1]**
Design and print your labels to meet NAFDAC's requirements (ingredients, warnings, expiry date, etc.).

**13. Oyo State business premises registration [7]**
Register your production premises with Oyo State's Ministry of Trade, Industry, Investment and Cooperatives.

**14. Trademark examination and acceptance [3]**
The Intellectual Property Office examines your trademark application.

**15. Trademark publication and opposition period [3]**
Your trademark is published, and there's a period for anyone to object. If no one does, you move forward.

**16. Trademark registration certificate [3]**
You receive your trademark certificate—your brand is now legally protected.

## Every year

You'll also need to renew your food handler medical tests, file CAC annual returns, and renew your Oyo State business premises registration each year. NAFDAC product registration and your trademark also need renewal on their schedules.

Registering a business name with CAC costs **₦10,000** and officially takes **24 working hours** [1]. That fee includes certified copies of your registration documents.

Before you register, you'll need to reserve your chosen name for ₦500, which takes about 4 working hours [1]. The reservation is valid for 60 days, so you have that long to complete the full registration.

You can do this online through the CAC's Company Registration Portal at https://icrp.cac.gov.ng/. You'll need to upload your NIN (or passport, driver's licence or voter's card), a passport photograph, your signature, and details about your business and residential address [1].

Keep in mind that CAC can change these fees and timelines, so confirm the current amounts on cac.gov.ng before you pay.

Here's your checklist in order. The steps are grouped by stage so you can see what comes first:

**Start here — you can do these now:**

1. Check that your product composition meets NAFDAC's Fruit Juice and Nectar Regulations [1]
2. Search for trademark availability to make sure your brand name isn't already taken [2]
3. Check whether your product needs SON MANCAP certification (optional but recommended) [3]
4. Make sure your production facility meets NAFDAC requirements [1]
5. Get your Federal Tax ID from the Nigeria Revenue Service [4]
6. Register with Oyo State tax authorities [4]
7. Arrange medical tests for your production staff (food handler tests) [1]

**Once you have your Federal Tax ID:**

8. File your trademark application [2]
9. Apply for MANCAP if your product needs it [3]
10. Register your business premises with Oyo State [5]

**Before NAFDAC can inspect your facility:**

You'll need your Federal Tax ID, your facility to be ready, and your staff to have passed their medical tests. Then NAFDAC will inspect and take samples for lab analysis.

**Before you can sell:**

NAFDAC will register your product once the lab analysis is done and your facility has passed inspection. After that, you'll need to get your labels approved and your trademark registered.

**Every year:**

You'll need to renew your CAC annual returns, renew your Oyo State premises registration, and renew your NAFDAC product registration.

Would you like me to go into detail on any of these steps, or shall we start with the first one?

**Sources**

1. NAFDAC requirements for packaged fruit drinks made in Nigeria (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nafdac.gov.ng](https://nafdac.gov.ng/food/guideline-for-micro-scale-enterprises/)
2. Trademark registration — Trademarks, Patents and Designs Registry (Nigerian Intellectual Property Office) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nipo.gov.ng](https://nipo.gov.ng/trademark.jsp)
3. Product certification for locally made products — Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) MANCAP (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [son.gov.ng](https://son.gov.ng/mancapservice/)
4. Tax registration — federal (NRS) and state internal revenue services (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [nrs.gov.ng](https://www.nrs.gov.ng/)
5. State business premises permits — Oyo, Lagos, FCT, Rivers, Ogun and Edo (information as of 25 Oct 2026) · [trade.oyostate.gov.ng](https://trade.oyostate.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/PROCEDURES-FOR-REGISTRATION-OF-BUSINESS-PREMISES.pdf)
6. Business registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) (information as of 24 Oct 2026) · [cac.gov.ng](https://www.cac.gov.ng/services/business-name)
